issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s repeated arrears in monthly rent can sustain eviction when the tenant relies on the absence of an agreed payment date or on depositing rent in the Treasury after the landlord refused payment.
material_facts: The tenant was found by the trial court to have been in arrears for more than two months on several occasions.
The courts below found that rent was payable month by month, despite there being no express agreement fixing the time for payment.
The tenant claimed that the landlord had refused rent and that the tenant had deposited rent in the Treasury; the trial court found those deposits ineffective under the amended law.
The tenant appealed the eviction decree, and the appellate courts’ findings were upheld as reasonable on the record.
issues.conclusion: The Court dismissed the appeal and left the eviction decree in force.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 11(1)(d) of the Bihar Building (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1947, as amended, the courts below treated repeated arrears of more than two months as a ground for eviction. The absence of an express agreement fixing the payment date did not excuse the tenant from paying rent regularly each month. Where a landlord refused rent, the trial court held that depositing it in the Treasury was ineffective and that the tenant’s course was to remit it by postal money order. The Supreme Court found the courts below’ findings reasonable; no earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: tenant_eviction_appeal and lower_courts_found_repeated_arrears and rent_was_payable_monthly and treasury_deposit_treated_as_ineffective

predicates.tenant_eviction_appeal: A tenant appealed a decree ordering eviction for rent default.
predicates.lower_courts_found_repeated_arrears: The courts below found that the tenant had been in arrears for more than two months on repeated occasions.
predicates.rent_was_payable_monthly: The courts below found that rent was payable regularly each month despite no express agreement fixing the payment date.
predicates.treasury_deposit_treated_as_ineffective: The tenant deposited rent in the Treasury after claiming that the landlord refused payment, and the trial court treated that method as ineffective.

issues.definition: When a tenant appeals an eviction decree, the courts below find repeated arrears of monthly rent, and the Treasury deposits relied on by the tenant are treated as ineffective, the eviction for rent default is upheld.
